## Experiment

`coop --git` with the step limit raised from 100 to 250 (compaction still at 28K). Tests whether the two agents finish once they have more time.

## Results

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Setting | `coop` with shared git, 2 agents per pair |
| Model | `gemini/gemini-3.8-flash`, high thinking |
| Subset | `flash_10` (10 pairs) |
| Step limit | 250 per agent |
| Compaction | at 28K tokens |
| Passed | 8/10 (80%) |
| Agents stopped at the step limit | 6 |
| Merge conflicts | 0 |
| Agent errors | 0 |
| Cost | `$19.87` (`$1.99` per pair) |
| Wall time | 124 min |

## Observations

- 8/10, all with cleanly merged patches. In `typst_task/6554` both agents pulled each other's work and ended with identical patches.
- In `dspy_task/8394` and `pallets_click_task/2800` one agent was later stopped at step 250, but it had already pushed its feature, so both features passed.
- `pallets_jinja_task/1559` and `pillow_task/290` failed: both agents were stopped at step 250 with nothing pushed, after summarizing their context 14 to 25 times.
- Data caveat: `duration_s` in `pairs.csv` is one hour too low for 4 pairs that ran across the daylight saving time change. The run's total wall time is correct.
